user_decision.question: Where should PR #8's re-keyed carrying table live -- in a shared non-private module both tactic families import, or in a register_lcarry environment-extension registry mirroring the merged view table? The draft asks the contributor for the shared module and names the registry alternative once so he can push back.
options: (a) A shared non-private module, e.g. FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/Carrying.lean, imported by Temporal.lean and Discrete.lean -- cheapest, a key change plus a file move, and the scope-core records add rows one line at a time

(b) A register_lcarry registry mirroring FormalSystem/Tactic/FormulaViews.lean's SimplePersistentEnvExtension -- lets the scope-core records add rows without touching any Temporal-family file at all, but the registration command must do its own checking since extension rows are invisible to the kernel and to #print axioms
user_decision.recommended: (a) A shared non-private module, e.g. FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/Carrying.lean, imported by Temporal.lean and Discrete.lean -- cheapest, a key change plus a file move, and the scope-core records add rows one line at a time

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic readme-lint gate is structurally blind in CI
sapience_notes.value: scripts/readme-lint.sh disables its Check 4 stale-date arm entirely under SHALLOW_CLONE=1, and actions/checkout is shallow by default. Measured on run 45112191590: the CI step printed 'Stale dates (info): (skipped: shallow clone, no history to date directories against)' then 'RESULT: PASS', while the identical script on the identical commit with full history reports 'FAIL (3 new stale dates)'. Every green CI readme-lint to date is therefore silent about stale dates rather than evidence about them; only a full-history local run can judge that gate.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic carrying-table reshape is the one real condition left on PR #8
sapience_notes.value: carryRules at FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/Temporal.lean:114-128 is private, holds two rows, and is keyed by a 'past' Bool plus one source operator, with the two target shapes hard-coded as the 'scope' and 'adjacent' fields. The scope-core records need a (source, target) key to express box facts carried by 4, 5, MF and TF into box, G and H scopes in both time directions. The value shape does NOT need to change: Perpetuity.boxToFuture, boxToPast and boxToBoxPast and their TM-plus mirrors already wrap into the existing proof-to-proof shape with the same ctxMp (thmIn ...) idiom futureKeep uses, and all three compile.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic: agent-system/ source store is absent from this checkout and poisons verify-touched.sh
sapience_notes.value: ls -d agent-system returns 'No such file or directory' in the BimodalLogic working tree, yet many .claude/scripts/tests suites build fixtures by copying from agent-system/extensions/core/**. The result is a standing, task-independent baseline: verify-touched.sh's narrowed battery reports 8 failing suites (test-force-phases, test-gate-cache-equivalence, test-gate-out-repair-reporting, test-loop-guard-budget-override, test-orchestrate-build-dispatch, test-postflight-deploy-gate, test-redeploy-checkpoint-promotion, test-roadmap-generation) with 'fixture is missing' assertions and rc=127, regardless of which files the dispatch actually touched. Attribute these away rather than treating them as a regression.

sapience_notes.subject: A mandatory PR head re-check at dispatch start is worth its cost on collaborator reviews
sapience_notes.value: On the BimodalLogic PR #8 re-review, the head moved between the plan round and the implement round, flipping mergeable from CONFLICTING to MERGEABLE and landing an entire follow-up the draft was about to request. Had the planned audit-only path run without the re-check, the posted response would have asked the contributor to do a rebase he had already done and to register views he had already registered. The re-check also halved the conditions of merging, from four to two.

sapience_notes.subject: A contributor editing records/ inside their own PR creates a reconciliation hazard
sapience_notes.value: PR #8 edits records/proof-mode-architecture.md (open decision 2 struck as settled, two 'Where the work sits' rows rewritten) and records/proof-mode.md (a 'Contributed in #8' bullet and an M4 semantic-argument paragraph) -- the same files a separate records-reconciliation task declares as its file_scope. The fix adopted was to invert the hand-off note so it leads with 'already landed by the PR, check before touching' and carries only the genuinely-ours milestones.md items as still owed, rather than carrying verbatim replacement text that would duplicate or revert the contributor's work.
